# Made by Human — extended context

Made by Human is a certification for physical products with verifiably human production. It focuses on whether essential, product-defining manufacturing steps are actually carried out by people and whether that production can be verified.

Official website: https://madebyhuman.org/
English website: https://madebyhuman.org/en/
Operator: D&G Handels GmbH, Paderborn, Germany
Official Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/madebyhuman.verify/
Official LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/made-by-human-org/

## Current normative framework

The current normative German standard is Made by Human Standard 1.0, published on 14 September 2026. Standard 1.0 is the first binding version intended for real certifications. Version 0.1 remains publicly available as an archived pre-release version.

Normative Standard 1.0: https://madebyhuman.org/dokumente/standard-1-0/
Certification Scheme 1.0: https://madebyhuman.org/dokumente/certification-scheme-1-0/
Standard overview: https://madebyhuman.org/standard/
Official documents and archived versions: https://madebyhuman.org/dokumente/

The English standard page is an informative translation for international readers. The published German Standard 1.0 is the normative reference.

## What the certification means

Certification applies to a clearly defined physical product or product family rather than automatically to an entire company. Production locations and important external manufacturing that materially affect the certified production process are part of the certification scope.

Product-defining manufacturing steps are steps that create or materially change the finished product's form, construction, function, surface, individual execution or another essential characteristic. Packaging, labelling, order picking, inspection or only minor finishing is not sufficient by itself.

Tools, machinery and digital systems may support manufacturing. Largely autonomous product creation does not meet the standard. All mandatory criteria applicable to the defined certification scope must be fulfilled.

A central decision question is: without the human production steps, would essentially the same sale-ready product already exist? If so, and no other essential human contribution shapes product creation, the product does not meet the standard.

## Verification model

A self-declaration alone is not sufficient. The Made by Human approach includes definition of the certification scope, documentation of the manufacturing process, suitable evidence, on-site review of the relevant production process, assessment against the applicable standard, technical review and a documented certification decision.

Approved certifications are published in a public register with a unique certification ID. The record identifies the product or product family, manufacturer or brand, relevant production locations, applicable standard version, certification status and validity.

A positive certification is normally valid for 12 months from the issue date. Before renewal, the certification is reassessed. The scope of reassessment depends on changes, previous findings and the production situation; a complete on-site audit is not automatically required every year but may be required.

Material changes to production steps, degree of automation, production locations, external manufacturing or certification scope must be reported. Made by Human then decides whether the certification can continue unchanged, needs additional assessment or extension, or must be suspended pending clarification.

## Certification status and mark use

The Made by Human mark may only be used for the expressly certified scope while the certification status is active. It must not imply certification of the whole company, non-certified products or additional properties that were not assessed. Suspended, expired or revoked certifications do not authorize continued mark use for the affected scope.

Mark use rules: https://madebyhuman.org/markennutzung/
Public register: https://madebyhuman.org/register/
Verify a certification: https://madebyhuman.org/pruefen/

## Connected applicants and transparency

Relevant legal, economic or personal relationships between the scheme owner, people involved in the assessment and an applicant are documented. When an applicant is connected to the scheme owner, that relationship is disclosed in the public certification record. Such cases are not described as independent third-party certification or as independently certified.

Made by Human does not claim accreditation or external independence unless such a property actually exists and can be substantiated.

Transparency: https://madebyhuman.org/transparenz/
Certification Scheme 1.0: https://madebyhuman.org/dokumente/certification-scheme-1-0/

## Scope boundaries

The certification is specifically about human production. It is not, by itself, a statement about sustainability, organic production, fair trade, country of origin, general product quality, product safety, regulatory compliance or company size.

Standard 1.0 does not currently include food, medicinal products, medical devices or comparably highly regulated product categories.
